title: Introduce TimeWarp RAG Simulator quickstart: synthetic user & structured-output linter
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Add TimeWarp RAG Simulator quickstart: local synthetic user runner, time-scaling probes, and structured-output linter to help teams validate RAG behaviors under varied latency/corpus profiles.
description: Motivation: Reproducing user-facing RAG regressions that depend on network latency, index freshness, or multi-tool interactions is time-consuming. This quickstart introduces the TimeWarp simulator — a lightweight local harness that lets engineers run deterministic, time-scaled RAG scenarios and assert structured outputs against expected contracts. The goal is a low-friction developer loop to reproduce flaky tool-calls, evaluate output stability under synthetic delays, and run quick regressions in CI. What this PR adds: 1) quickstarts/timewarp-simulator/README.md — end-to-end guide and expected workflows; 2) a compact TypeScript runner (runner/ts/) that drives synthetic user sessions with configurable latency/timewarp factors and replayable corpora; 3) a structured-output linter (examples/linting/structured-output-linter.py) that validates JSON/YAML responses against field-level contracts and fuzzy string expectations; 4) telemetry probes (telemetry/probes.yaml) and a CI smoke job (ci/smoke-timewarp.yml) that runs a short scenario on PRs to catch regressions; 5) docs site registration (docs/quickstarts.yml and docs/snippets/timewarp-setup.md) so quickstart appears in the docs sidebar. Security & privacy: The runner uses seedable, local-only corpora (examples/playback/sample-corpus.json) and never ships customer data; a note in the README explains sanitization for real-indexed corpora. Quickstart highlights and commands: - Install node and python (README includes minimal versions). - From the quickstart dir: npm ci && npm run build && node dist/run.js --corpus examples/playback/sample-corpus.json --timewarp 0.5 --seed 42 This runs a session that simulates accelerated token/latency pacing (0.5x wall clock). - To run with a 2x slow-down: --timewarp 2.0 - Lint responses: python3 examples/linting/structured-output-linter.py --input out/session-001.json --schema quickstarts/timewarp-simulator/contracts/session-schema.yaml - CI smoke: ci/smoke-timewarp.yml runs the runner against a short scenario and fails the job if structured-output linter finds contract divergences. Developer notes & checklist: - ✅ Deterministic seeds added to runner and sample corpus for reproducibility. - ✅ Minimal telemetry hooks (span ids + latency histograms) added so SRE can wire into existing dashboards. - ✅ Docs snippets and usage examples included with copyable CLI commands. - ✅ Small sample corpus and a guide for sanitizing real corpora are included. - Known limitations: The simulator is not a substitute for full-scale load testing; it targets functional/regression scenarios and structured-output stability. It currently supports HTTP-based tool stubs and the Redwood hosted API compatibility layer; adding grpc tool stubs is tracked in ENG-3330. Migration/upgrade notes: The quickstart is opt-in; it does not change runtime behavior. To adopt, teams can copy the quickstart folder into their repos or reference the runner as a submodule. Linear tickets: ENG-3214 tracks simulator enhancements and instrumentation; PM-78 tracks product docs and a short tutorial. Testing & CI summary: A new smoke CI job was added and is gated on docs and lint passing on PRs touching quickstarts. Full unit tests live alongside the runner and were executed as part of this PR's CI. Merge summary: squash-merged to main after reviewers signed off and CI green.
